PullRequest.Title: Show a fallback message when the web workbench fails to start
PullRequest.Body: Fixes the blank-page failure mode reported in #337226. ### Problem When the bootstrap scripts never run, the web workbench renders nothing and the user gets a blank white page. The only signal is `Cannot determine URI for module id!` in the console, which points nowhere near the actual cause. This happens whenever something between the server and the browser blocks or rewrites the page scripts — a reverse proxy, a content filter, a corporate TLS-inspecting middlebox, a browser extension, or a blocked CDN. #337226 hit it via an edge optimizer that neutralizes `

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing server-side template read/render and HTML response complete before browser parsing; the browser parses the added inline CSS and three fallback nodes while existing CSS/NLS/workbench module requests proceed. After the workbench module graph has loaded and evaluated, the entry IIFE removes the fallback before creating the workbench. The removal is on startup's critical path but is one ID lookup and one three-node subtree removal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected production workbench HTML template for rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing template read per workbench document request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same template file was read once and rendered for every workbench document request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read is on the existing server response critical path; the diff only increases this small template by roughly the added static CSS/markup and does not add another read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return the rendered workbench HTML document to the browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing HTML response per top-level navigation; payload gains one constant-size style block and three elements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single HTML response was sent without the fallback CSS and markup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added constant payload must be transferred and parsed before startup, but it is small and does not scale with user data. Existing linked CSS, manifest, NLS, and module requests are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load existing linked CSS, manifest, NLS modules, and workbench module.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same fixed set of resource requests per navigation, subject to normal browser caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical linked-resource requests occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The workbench module remains on the startup critical path; the diff neither adds a request nor changes request ordering or concurrency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fallback style block and one three-node subtree per top-level navigation, independent of workspace size, extension count, editor count, or session lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing browser-managed fetching of stylesheet, manifest, NLS modules, and the workbench module is unchanged. The diff adds no tasks, promises, worker/process creation, queue, limiter, or concurrent boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The dynamically rendered HTML is still generated per navigation and has no newly changed cache policy. Existing browser caching for linked resources is unchanged. There is no fallback cache key, miss path, retry, or coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the complete changed hunks and startup/server call path show fixed-size markup/CSS, an existing response boundary, and immediate subtree removal once the entry module executes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact added transfer and style/DOM processing time varies with compression and browser, but the added work is a small fixed amount and has no realistic scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds negligible constant startup work and cleans up its temporary DOM subtree on successful bootstrap.

Scenarios.Scenario: Production web workbench navigation where scripts are blocked or rewritten
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing HTML request and parse complete, then the browser holds the hidden fallback and schedules one zero-duration visibility animation for 10 seconds. Because scripts do not execute, no workbench-module critical path progresses; the fallback becomes visible after the delay without waiting for any additional request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return the rendered workbench HTML containing the self-contained fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing document response per failed navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same document response occurred, but contained no fallback message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response is required to display the fallback, but the diff adds no follow-up request; script blocking is external to the changed code.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One animation and three DOM nodes per failed page/tab. Cost is constant per tab and does not grow with retries, workspace contents, events, or elapsed time beyond retaining the tiny static subtree for that document's lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One independent browser animation per failed tab; no polling, repeated timer, task fan-out, IPC, subprocess, or application-level concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The fallback intentionally requires no additional resource and therefore has no cold/warm cache distinction. Existing document and attempted script-resource cache behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: all fallback assets are inline, and no script executes on this path, so there is no hidden transitive boundary or repeated application work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser implementation details may vary for scheduling a delayed discrete CSS animation, but it is a single constant-size animation and retained subtree per failed tab.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Retention and animation scheduling are deliberately bounded to one tiny static fallback per failed document.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The development server performs the existing template read/render and CSS-module discovery, sends the document, and the browser runs the existing import-map/CSS-module bootstrap before loading the workbench entry. The added fallback is parsed once and removed at entry-module evaluation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the development workbench template after existing CSS-module discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing template read per development workbench request; CSS-module discovery cardinality is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The development template was read once per request without fallback markup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing template read remains on the response critical path; only a small constant number of bytes are added to the file.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send development HTML and load the existing workbench module/CSS imports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HTML response plus the same existing module and generated CSS resource requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same development bootstrap and resource loading occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing module/CSS loads remain on the development startup path. The diff adds no request and does not multiply the CSS-module loop.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added work remains one fixed style block and three nodes per navigation. Existing CSS-module cardinality may scale with development modules, but the diff does not alter that loop or its data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing CSS-module discovery and browser module loading remain unchanged; the fallback adds no boundary calls or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Development resource caching behavior and CSS-module generation are unchanged. The fallback is inline and has no cache, retry, or coalescing state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the complete development-template hunk only adds fixed inline content, and the unchanged bootstrap shows all scaling work predates the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Development import-map and CSS-module costs vary by checkout, but none of their cardinality or scheduling is changed by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added development-startup work is fixed-size and temporary.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced successful, blocked-script, and development startup paths through server template reads, HTML delivery, browser resource loading, CSS animation scheduling, and DOM cleanup. The change introduces only small constant per-navigation parsing/allocation and no new expensive boundary, fan-out, repeated work, concurrency burst, or unbounded retention.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
